about.title: Windsor Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Windsor sits along corridors like Old Redwood Highway and US-101, where residents commute, shop, and bring home everyday products — appliances, tools, vehicle parts, children's items — that are supposed to be safe. When a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing mistake, or a missing warning, California's strict liability rules generally mean you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the defect existed and caused harm. That distinction matters in Sonoma County, where a defective product could trace back to a local retailer, a regional distributor, or a manufacturer states away. If a product has hurt you or someone in your household here, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of injury can matter for any later claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect injured Windsor residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options with no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Windsor Product Liability Case

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims to proceed under strict liability, meaning the focus stays on whether the product was defective rather than on proving carelessness.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the item in Windsor can potentially be held liable, which widens the field of who may be accountable.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves the Evidence
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on the physical defect itself, keeping the product intact and unaltered after an injury can be critical to how an attorney evaluates your case.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability framework, you generally need to show the product had a defect and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless. This can make the path to a claim more direct than typical negligence cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Does it matter that I live in Windsor specifically?
items.answer: Where you live doesn't change the underlying California law, but it can affect where a claim is filed and which local records, such as purchase receipts from a Windsor retailer, might be relevant. An independent attorney can walk you through what applies to your situation.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
